question: ‘Along The Red River: A Memoir’ is a book about the life of _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sabita Goswami.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ‘Along The Red River: A Memoir’ is a powerful **autobiography** of the acclaimed veteran journalist, Sabita Goswami.
 
• This book documents the extraordinary, **single-handed fight** of an **ordinary woman in the heart of Assam**, against family and social **obstacles,** to establish herself emotionally and professionally.
 
• Sabita Goswami began as a **freelance** journalist in **Assam in 1972.**
 
• She is the** first woman** to be **associated with global news agencies** like the AFP and BBC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nirupama Borgohain** is a **Sahitya Akademi Award winner** and is best known for her novel **'Abhiyatri'**.

 
 
• She was a recipient of the** Assam Valley Literary Award.**
 
• Her novels are mainly based on realism where she has consciously dealt with the problem of **inequality** that exists between men and women in society.
 
 
 
• **Mitra Phukan** is an Indian author who writes in English.
 
 
• She has received so far the **UNICEF-CBT Award** for children's fiction, the Katha Award for Translation
 
• The **Telegraph-Vineet Gupta Memorial Award** for short fiction.
 
 
 
• ** Pushpalata Das**(1915–2003) was an Indian independence activist, and social worker.
 
 
• She was a Gandhian and legislator from the north-east Indian state of Assam.
 
• She was awarded the** Padma Bhushan** by the Indian Government, in** 1999**, for her role in India's freedom struggle.
